They mine coal used to make steel in Alabama mines and sell it to steel makers in Europe, South America and Asia.
The new Blue Creek mine started in October 2025, eight months early, raising yearly capacity to 13.7 million metric tons.
Coal prices are only set for short stretches, so their sales rise and fall with the global steel market.
Risks they name: weak steel demand, record Chinese steel exports, too much coal supply, tariffs, and steel makers using substitutes.

takeaways: The new mine is paying off so far: more coal sold and more profit this quarter.
Not everything improved: cost per ton went up, and shipping costs and port delays cut into what they got paid.
This business depends on steel demand and coal prices, which swing up and down, and future special dividends are not promised.

earnings.headline: Home Depot's sales and profit both grew this quarter and beat the company's own expectations, but fewer shoppers came in.
points: Sales (money from customers) were $43.4 billion, up 4.9% from the same quarter a year ago.
Profit was $3.7 billion, or $3.72 per share, up from $3.62 per share a year ago.
Fewer shoppers: comparable customer visits fell 0.5%, but the average purchase rose 3.0% to $93.09.
Their own forecast (guidance) for the year: sales up about 4.5%, per-share profit up about 1.5%.
They sell home improvement goods, building supplies and garden products in 2,359 stores, online, and to pros.
In fiscal 2025 sales rose 3.2% to $164.7 billion, mostly from buying two supply companies, SRS and GMS.
Profit got worse: per-share earnings were $14.23, down from $14.91 the year before.
Risks they name: tough competition, harm to their brand, and tariffs (taxes on imported goods).
Several headlines say the stock rose a lot before earnings and ask whether it now costs too much.
Barron's says earnings beat Wall Street's estimates, but the incoming new CEO (top boss) got the attention.
CNBC says a slow housing market has been holding the company back.

takeaways: Home Depot is still growing sales and profit, but slowly, and fewer people are shopping there.
Much of its recent growth came from buying other companies, not just from its own stores.
A slow housing market, tariffs and competition are real risks, and new leaders are taking over.

points: Shareholders approved Bagchi's appointment at the bank, a leadership decision put to a shareholder vote.
The bank's staff stock options and units vest in four stages, meaning employees earn them bit by bit over time.
Headlines say the share price rose 22% over a stretch and hit a 3-month high, though one notes heavy selling pressure too.

takeaways: No earnings report or annual report text was provided, so there is no official sales or profit news to explain here.
The headlines are mostly about the share price and a leadership vote, not about how the bank's business is doing.
Some headlines push opinions on the stock; those are views from outside writers, not facts from the company.

earnings.headline: HII had record quarterly sales and much higher profit, and raised its own forecast for 2026 shipbuilding sales.
points: Sales (revenue) hit a record $3.5 billion for the quarter, up 10.8% from the same quarter last year.
Profit (net earnings) was $217 million, up from $145 million. Per share it was $5.48, up from $3.68.
Their own forecast (guidance) for 2026 shipbuilding sales rose to $10.5 to $10.7 billion, from $10.2B to $10.4B before.
Weak spot: Ingalls (the non-nuclear shipyard) earned $59 million, down from $65 million, due to weaker work on warships.
HII is America's largest shipbuilder. It builds Navy ships, including nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers, plus defense tech.
Almost all of its business comes from the U.S. Government, mainly the Department of War. That is its biggest dependence.
This year brought a 43-day government shutdown, but Congress also set aside more than $29 billion for shipbuilding.
Risks they name: not enough skilled workers, supplier delays, rising costs (inflation), and federal budget fights.
One article says a surge in shipbuilding work led to stronger earnings.
Most other headlines are stock forecasts and analyst opinions, not news from the company itself.

takeaways: The company is growing: record sales, higher profit, and $32.4 billion in new contracts this quarter.
They say about 90 percent of the shipbuilding sales they expect through 2030 is already covered by contracts.
Not all good: one shipyard earned less, and the business leans almost fully on U.S. government spending.
